name: United States
summary: Three national MNOs (T-Mobile, AT&T, Verizon) after T-Mobile absorbed UScellular's wireless business (2025) and EchoStar sold its terrestrial spectrum to AT&T (closed July 2026) and SpaceX (pending), leaving Boost Mobile as a hybrid MVNO. Licences are geographic (CMA/BTA/MTA/EA/PEA/county), so figures are FCC population-weighted averages adjusted for transactions closed by 2026-09-28.

operators.name: AT&T
operators.legal: AT&T Mobility / New Cingular Wireless PCS, LLC
operators.notes: Operates FirstNet (Band 14, licensed to the First Responder Network Authority) under a 25-year contract from 2017. Bought UScellular/Array 3.45 GHz + Lower 700 MHz licences (closed 2026-01-13) and EchoStar's 3.45 GHz + 600 MHz licences (FCC approval 2026-05-12, closed 2026-07-28).

operators.name: Verizon
operators.notes: Bought Array (ex-UScellular) cellular/AWS/PCS licences for $1.0bn (FCC approval 2026, closed 2026-06-01). Largest winner of AWS-3 Auction 113 (June 2026, 82 licences, $3.16bn gross); those licences not yet reflected.

operators.name: T-Mobile
operators.notes: Merged with Sprint 2020-04-01 (BRS/EBS 2.5 GHz, PCS G block). Acquired UScellular's wireless operations and ~30% of its spectrum (600 MHz, 2.5 GHz, 24 GHz and most 700 A/AWS/PCS) on 2025-08-01, plus further Array 700/600 MHz licences in May 2026. Sold its 3.45 GHz licences (SoniqWave swap 2024; N77 License Co/Columbia Capital 2025). Swapped its 800 MHz SMR licences to Grain for $2.9bn + Grain's 600 MHz licences (closed 2026-08-10). Acquires Comcast's 600 MHz licences in stages (accelerated portion closed 2026-06-02; rest targeted 1H 2028; already leased).

operators.name: EchoStar (Boost Mobile)
operators.legal: EchoStar Corporation (DISH Network subsidiaries; Northstar/SNR for AWS-3)
operators.notes: Sold all 3.45 GHz and 600 MHz licences to AT&T (closed 2026-07-28); Boost is becoming a hybrid MVNO on AT&T. AWS-4, H-block and unpaired AWS-3 (1695-1710) licences were transferred to a trust on 2026-05-22 pending the Spectrum Acquisition Closing with SpaceX (targeted 2027-11-30). Retains Lower 700 E, paired AWS-3, CBRS PALs and mmWave.

operators.name: Array (ex-UScellular)
operators.legal: Array Digital Infrastructure, Inc. (formerly United States Cellular Corporation)
operators.notes: Wireless operations sold to T-Mobile 2025-08-01; now a tower company holding residual spectrum (mainly C-band, CBRS, 28/37/39 GHz) that it seeks to monetise. TDS made a take-private proposal on 2026-05-07.

operators.name: Grain (NewLevel)
operators.legal: NEWLEVEL IV, L.P. / Grain Management, LLC
operators.notes: Acquired T-Mobile's 800 MHz SMR (B26) licences 2026-08-10; plans leasing incl. direct-to-device.

operators.name: SpaceX (Starlink)
operators.notes: Buying EchoStar's AWS-4, H-block and unpaired AWS-3 licences (FCC approval 2026-05-12; licences held in trust since 2026-05-22; acquisition closing targeted 2027-11-30). Won 2 licences in Auction 113.

operators.name: Comcast (Xfinity Mobile)
operators.notes: MVNO on Verizon. Holds CBRS PALs; its 600 MHz licences are leased to and being sold to T-Mobile (partial close 2026-06-02, rest 1H 2028).

operators.name: Charter (Spectrum Mobile)
operators.notes: MVNO on Verizon; holds CBRS PALs used for offload. Acquired Cox Communications (closed 2026-08-19); the company is to be renamed Cox Communications, keeping the Spectrum brand.

notes: Licensing is geographic (CMA, BTA/MTA, EA, REAG, PEA, county). All holdings are population-weighted national averages in MHz per direction for FDD. Base data: FCC 2024 Communications Marketplace Report (FCC 24-136), Figs. II.B.14/II.B.16, staff estimates as of June 2024 (regulator source). Adjustments for later transactions are this file's estimates, using the pop-weighted holdings of the seller and the scope stated in the FCC approval orders.

Transactions reflected (closed by 2026-09-28): T-Mobile/UScellular wireless ops + 600/700A/AWS/PCS/2.5/24 GHz (2025-08-01); T-Mobile 3.45 GHz sales to SoniqWave and N77 License Co (2024-25); AT&T/Array 3.45 GHz + Lower 700 (2026-01-13); Array 700/600 MHz to T-Mobile (May 2026); Verizon/Array cellular, AWS, PCS (2026-06-01); T-Mobile/Comcast 600 MHz accelerated tranche (2026-06-02, amount not quantified); AT&T/EchoStar 3.45 GHz + 600 MHz (2026-07-28); T-Mobile/Grain 800 MHz for 600 MHz swap (2026-08-10).

Pending: EchoStar AWS-4, H-block and unpaired AWS-3 to SpaceX — FCC approved 2026-05-12, licences in trust since 2026-05-22, closing targeted 2027-11-30 (future entries). Comcast 600 MHz remainder to T-Mobile targeted 1H 2028 (already leased to T-Mobile). Auction 113 (AWS-3 re-auction) licences: winners announced 2026-06-26, not added.
Upper C-band (3.98-4.2 GHz): auction required by 2025 legislation, not yet held (background knowledge, not source-verified).

Cross-check: PolicyTracker gives Verizon 279 MHz pop-weighted excluding mmWave (matches CMR 278.9) and AT&T 375 MHz after the EchoStar deal. This file gives AT&T ≈ 338 MHz sub-6 GHz incl. FirstNet B14 (≈318 without), Verizon ≈ 280 excl. CBRS, T-Mobile ≈ 356 — the gap likely reflects leased 3.45 GHz and different band scopes; FCC figures preferred.
FCC DA 26-470 (AT&T-EchoStar): post-transaction AT&T holds ≥1/3 of below-1-GHz spectrum in 354 CMAs (~65% of pop) and up to 100 MHz of 3.45 GHz in some markets.
The FCC CMR attributes partnership spectrum to multiple holders; cellular (850) amounts were scaled to the 25 MHz per-direction band size.
T-Mobile's 2025 license swaps with AT&T (PCS/AWS/700/600/2.5 GHz, many markets) and Verizon (Kentucky) rationalise holdings market by market and are not modelled.
missing: Exact block positions: not compiled (licences vary by market); holdings only.
Post-June-2024 amounts are estimates: splits of UScellular/Array spectrum between T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon approximated from the FCC orders' scope, not from ULS MHz-pop calculations.
CBRS PAL pop-weighted holdings are rough estimates (Verizon derived from coverage; EchoStar, Comcast, Charter not source-verified); other PAL holders omitted.
Auction 113 (AWS-3) winning licences not added: per-licence MHz-pops and grant status not confirmed.
Comcast 600 MHz holdings (leased to T-Mobile) not separated from 'Others'.
Split of AT&T's 700 MHz holding between paired B/C and D/E SDL is estimated.
Upper C-band status and 4.9 GHz band-manager details from background knowledge, not source-verified.
